fields.h1: Build a Nonprofit Landing Page for Every Gift and Signup
fields.hero_description: Build a nonprofit landing page from a prompt that takes gifts, fills volunteer shifts, and saves each one to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Behind the Donate Button
fields.features_subheading: Each nonprofit landing page Emergent builds has these six parts, covering the gift itself and what happens after it.
fields.feature_1:
A page written from your campaign brief

Describe the cause and the ask in plain English. Emergent builds the page with its gift form and the database table behind it, and rewrites any section when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
A goal bar that moves with each gift

The goal bar and the running gift count update live as gifts arrive. A Giving Tuesday push or a year-end appeal gets one number that supporters and staff can both watch.
fields.feature_3:
Gifts through the Stripe account you have

Connect the Stripe account the nonprofit already takes donations with. Each completed gift comes back to the page's database with the amount and the campaign it belongs to.
fields.feature_4:
Supporter records in a database you own

Every donor and volunteer becomes a row in a database you own, tagged with the page they came from. Sync those rows to HubSpot or any CRM with an API instead of retyping them.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts for the moments that need a person

Choose the moments that deserve a human follow-up, such as a large gift or a shift that has filled. The page posts each one to Slack or emails the one person who handles it.
fields.feature_6:
Your own domain, and the code to keep

Publish under the nonprofit's own domain, which is included and runs on credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository for a developer to extend.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Nonprofit Pages, Each With One Ask
fields.tab_content_1:
Each gift counts twice until $10,000 of match is gone

Tallow Creek Food Bank set one Giving Tuesday goal: $30,000 by midnight. A board member matches every gift from a $10,000 pool. A $100 gift counts as $200, and the page shows $3,900 of the match still left. Gifts go through the Stripe account the food bank connects and save to its gifts table.
fields.tab_content_2:
When a shift hits 20 volunteers, it closes

Hollis Bend River Trust needs two shifts of 20 volunteers for a Saturday cleanup. Each volunteer picks a shift, accepts the waiver, and lands in the volunteers table. Once the 9 AM shift is full, the page offers only 1 PM, which has 6 spots left. On Friday at 5 PM, coordinator Teodora Ibarra gets both rosters by email.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every runner gets a page and a $300 goal

For the Quarry Street 5K, Pinehollow Reading Project gives each registered runner a personal page with a $300 goal. Gifts made there count toward the runner and the team. When Dara Fennimore reached $315 from 9 gifts, her page marked the goal met and emailed her a thank-you.
fields.tab_content_4:
Letter gifts of $500 or more reach the director

Mossgate Animal Rescue mails its year-end letter with a QR code for each donor. The code opens the gift page with that donor's last gift filled in, and each gift saves with the appeal code MAIL-DEC. Any gift of $500 or more sends director Ondine Bancroft a Slack message for a thank-you call. The latest was $650.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Nonprofit Landing Page
fields.howto_description: These seven steps take a nonprofit landing page from a single ask to a published page that saves each gift and signup.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the page asks for
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the case in three short lines
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the amounts and the goal
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the page in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick one action: a gift, a volunteer shift, or a race registration. Give it a deadline, even a soft one. Write the ask as one sentence a supporter could repeat, because it becomes the headline and the opening line of your prompt.
fields.howto_step_2_des: State the need and what one gift does about it, then the date it matters by. Use a figure from your own program records, such as families served last winter, instead of a national statistic you cannot trace.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose three or four gift amounts from what donors gave in your last campaign, and preselect the middle one. Set a goal you can reach by the deadline, and decide whether a matched gift counts once or twice toward it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the ask and the case into one prompt, and say where gifts should go. Emergent returns a working page with its form and gifts table. Ask for the thank-you screen in the same prompt: what the donor sees right after giving.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect the Stripe account that receives donations, then HubSpot or another CRM with an API. Decide which fields each tool should receive, starting with the donor email and the gift amount. Map them once here instead of fixing records by hand after the campaign.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Make a test gift from your phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give $5 on your own phone and follow it all the way through: the row in the gifts table, the receipt email, the Slack alert, and the CRM record. Fix anything missing before a single supporter sees the page.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish with an appeal code per link
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page, then give the email link and the social link their own appeal codes. After the first week, compare gifts by code in the gifts table and put more effort where the money came from.

faq_plan.q: What is a nonprofit landing page?
faq_plan.a: A nonprofit landing page is a standalone page built for one action a supporter can take, such as giving, signing up for a volunteer shift, or registering for a charity run. Leave out the main site's menu and keep the form in view; the page then records who acted and which campaign brought them.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a nonprofit landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the campaign to Emergent's AI landing page builder in a few sentences: who the gift helps, the deadline, and the amounts to offer. Read the first version the way a donor would, top to bottom, before you publish it.

faq_plan.q: What should a Giving Tuesday landing page include?
faq_plan.a: It needs a reason the day matters this year, such as a match that expires at midnight, and one line on what the total buys. Say which time zone that midnight is in. Plan the morning after as well: swap the headline for a thank-you with the final total, and leave the form open for late gifts.

faq_plan.q: Should a donation landing page have a video?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you have a short clip of the work a gift pays for, such as a volunteer stocking a pantry shelf. Place it beside the gift form so the form stays in view, and keep it under a minute. When the clip carries the whole appeal, build a video landing page with the donate button right under the player.

faq_plan.q: What are some good donation landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Four patterns are worth copying beyond the ones above. A monthly giving page sets the monthly option as the default. An emergency appeal names the crisis and the date the money is needed by. A tribute page asks whose name the gift honors and who should be told. A capital campaign page shows the building goal and what each amount pays for.

faq_plan.q: Should nonprofit landing pages use the main website's domain?
faq_plan.a: Yes, where you can. A subdomain such as give.example.org keeps the address donors already know and matches the sender of your emails. Custom domains come included with Emergent and use credits.

faq_plan.q: Should donation landing pages also sign people up for events?
faq_plan.a: No. Move the event invitation to the screen after the gift instead. Put an online briefing for donors on its own webinar landing page and link it from the thank-you email, where signing up no longer competes with giving.

faq_plan.q: When should Giving Tuesday landing pages go live?
faq_plan.a: Publish them at least a week before the day. Giving Tuesday falls on the Tuesday after Thanksgiving in the United States, which is December 1 in 2026. A week of lead time lets reminder emails point to a page that already works, and early gifts start the progress bar above zero.

faq_plan.q: What should a non profit landing page send after a gift?
faq_plan.a: It should send a receipt by email as soon as the gift goes through. The IRS says the written acknowledgment for a contribution of $250 or more must contain the name of the organization and the amount of the cash contribution. Put both on every receipt, whatever the amount. The page Emergent builds can send that email and keep each receipt in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a charity landing page work on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Put the gift amounts and the donate button on the first screen, sized for a thumb, and ask only for a name, an email, and the card. The rules of any mobile landing page apply: a single column and nothing that covers the form.

findings.quote: The IRS says the written acknowledgment for a contribution of $250 or more must contain the name of the organization and the amount of the cash contribution. Put both on every receipt, whatever the amount.
findings.issue: The fact is true (items 1-2 of the IRS list), but the advice that follows names only those two. The same IRS list also requires a statement that no goods or services were provided, or a good-faith estimate of their value. A nonprofit that copies the advice would send $250+ receipts that are missing a required line.
findings.fix: Add the third element, e.g. 'Put both on every receipt, with a line saying whether the donor received anything in return.'

findings.quote: GivingTuesday is the Tuesday after Thanksgiving in the United States
findings.issue: Both quoted spans are narrower than the copy. FAQ 8's 'December 1 in 2026' is in the Wikipedia infobox ('2026 date: December 1'), not in the quoted sentence. FAQ 9's 'name of the organization' and 'amount of cash contribution' sit in the list under the IRS quote ('...must contain'), not in it. I checked both on the source pages (2026-10-14) and both hold. Wikipedia is also not a primary source.
findings.fix: Widen the quotes to the spans that state the copy (the infobox date; the IRS list items), and prefer givingtuesday.org for the date.

findings.quote: Give $5 on your own phone and follow it all the way through: the row in the gifts table, the receipt email, the Slack alert, and the CRM record.
findings.issue: On this page, Slack alerts fire only for chosen moments ('such as a large gift', feature_5; '$500 or more', tab_content_4). A $5 test gift would not trigger the Slack alert the step tells the reader to check.
findings.fix: '...the receipt email, the CRM record, and the Slack alert if you lower its threshold for the test.' Or drop the Slack alert from the list.

findings.issue: The tab 4 Slack hero draws the recipient with a channel hash ('# Ondine Bancroft'). The copy says director Ondine Bancroft gets a Slack message, so it should read as a direct message, not a channel.
findings.fix: Render a person recipient as a DM (avatar or initials, no '#'), or make the engine drop the hash when the channel field is a person's name.

findings.quote: When a shift reaches 20, take it off the page and show the spots left on the other one.
findings.issue: The mockup prompt (and plan) say the full shift leaves the page, but the tab 2 image keeps a '9 AM, full' slot visible. The tab copy ('the page offers only 1 PM') agrees with the image, so the drift is between the prompt and the drawing, not the copy.
findings.fix: Change the prompt to 'mark it full so no one can pick it'.

findings.quote: Leave out the main site's menu and keep the form in view; the page then records who acted and which campaign brought them.
findings.issue: The definition answer switches to an instruction mid-answer, and 'then' makes recording sound like a result of hiding the menu. That is two ideas joined by a semicolon.
findings.fix: 'It leaves out the main site's menu and keeps the form in view. The page records who acted and which campaign brought them.'

findings.quote: saves each one to a database you own
findings.issue: The database-you-own idea appears in four fields: hero_description 'saves each one to a database you own'; feature_4 'Every donor and volunteer becomes a row in a database you own'; why_description 'Gifts and volunteer signups land in a database you own'; FAQ 9 'keep each receipt in a database you own'.
findings.fix: Keep it in the hero and feature_4. Elsewhere, name a concrete consequence instead (e.g. why_description on editing the page by prompt only).
